metadata.title: Xavier Smith signs with 49ers
metadata.description: The 49ers signed WR Xavier Smith to the practice squad.
metadata.analysis: Smith will add depth at wide receiver and on special teams in the return game for San Francisco.

metadata.title: Xavier Smith - Heads to Bay Area on practice squad
metadata.description: The 49ers signed Smith to the practice squad Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Smith was cut by the Rams on Friday, but the Florida A&M product will stay in the NFC West division with the 49ers as a member of the practice squad. Smith would be a top candidate for an elevation to the active roster if the 49ers needed more depth at wide receiver.

metadata.title: Xavier Smith - Cut by Los Angeles
metadata.description: The Rams waived Smith on Friday.
metadata.analysis: Smith played 38 offensive snaps and ran 32 routes last Sunday night against the Broncos but wasn't targeted by Matthew Stafford and has drawn just one target on 60 routes through three weeks. He's also returned seven punts for 69 yards and seven kicks for 144 yards.

metadata.title: Xavier Smith - Draws just one target Monday
metadata.description: Smith did not catch his only target during Monday's 28-6 win versus the Giants, but he recorded four punt returns for 32 yards and two kickoff returns for 29 yards.
metadata.analysis: With usual lead target Puka Nacua (groin) out, Smith was actually the Rams' third option at wide receiver in Week 2 in terms of offensive snaps (25) behind 2025 seventh-rounder Konata Mumpfield (42) and veteran Davante Adams (38), but Adams was the only Rams wideout who saw more than two targets. Smith remained heavily involved on special teams, however, and that will probably continue to be his primary function as long as one of Nacua or Adams is in pads.

metadata.title: Xavier Smith - Plays 16 offensive snaps in Week 1
metadata.description: Smith played 16 of 61 offensive snaps in the Rams' 27-7 loss to the 49ers in Week 1 and didn't record any touches or targets.
metadata.analysis: Smith is the Rams' punt returner and returned one for 11 yards. He also gained 25 yards on one kick return. His offensive snaps were elevated late in the game when the Rams pulled their starters. Smith has next to no fantasy value.

metadata.title: Xavier Smith signs exclusive rights tender Monday
metadata.description: Xavier Smith has signed his exclusive rights free agent tender to remain with the Rams for the upcoming 2026 campaign.
metadata.analysis: After catching two passes for six yards in 15 games as a rookie in 2024, Smith broke out for an 18-303-0 receiving line last season. He also handles return duties, averaging 23.2 yards on 13 kickoff returns and 9.3 yards on 27 punt returns a season ago. Smith will likely see a similar role in 2026, but can step into a starting gig at receiver should a need arise.

metadata.title: Xavier Smith - Signs tender with Rams
metadata.description: Smith signed his exclusive-rights tender with the Rams on Monday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
metadata.analysis: Smith signed a $1.075 million tender to remain with the Rams in 2026. The depth wide receiver is all set to suit up as a special teams player who also can provide offensive utility for quarterback Matthew Stafford. Smith hauled in 18 receptions for 303 yards over 16 regular-season contests in 2025, a significant improvement from his two receptions for six yards in the Rams' 2024 campaign.

metadata.title: Xavier Smith tendered by Rams
metadata.description: Xavier Smith has been tendered by the Rams and will return to Los Angeles for the 2026 season.
metadata.analysis: Smith saw his role expand in his second season in the NFL last year as he finished with 18 catches for 303 yards over 16 regular season contests. He was also a key component on special teams, racking up 301 kickoff return yards and 251 punt return yards on the year. Smith will likely fill a similar role for the Rams in 2026.

metadata.title: Xavier Smith - Tendered by Rams
metadata.description: The Rams tendered Smith on Monday.
metadata.analysis: Smith was slated to be an exclusive rights free agent, and by receiving a tender, he's now locked in with Los Angeles for another season. The Florida A&M product has served as a depth wideout for the Rams during his two campaigns in the NFL, and he saw his role expand last year with an 18-303-0 receiving line over 16 regular-season games. Smith also was a key component of the Rams' special-teams unit, racking up 301 kick-return yards and 251 punt-return yards. He'll likely be deployed in a similar role next season.

metadata.title: Rams Tender Contracts to Harrison Mevis, Xavier Smith
metadata.description: The Los Angeles Rams announced on Monday that they tendered exclusive-rights free-agent kicker Harrison Mevis and wide receiver Xavier Smith. Neither Mevis nor Smith will be allowed to negotiate with other teams this offseason. Mevis, 23, made his NFL debut last year and was impressive, making 12 of his 13 field-goal attempts (made his lone try from 50-plus yards) and all 39 of his extra-point tries in nine regular-season games. He finished the year ranked as the No. 8 fantasy kicker in terms of fantasy points per game at 8.3. In the playoffs, Mevis was a perfect 15-for-15 on field goals (six) and extra-point tries. The former undrafted kicker out of Missouri should enter the 2026 season as the favorite to be L.A.'s starting kicker, which will make him pretty attractive in fantasy football in one of the league's highest-scoring offenses.

metadata.title: Xavier Smith - Little impact in win
metadata.description: Smith secured one of two targets for six yards, returned one punt for nine yards and returned one kickoff for 27 yards during Sunday's 37-20 victory over the Cardinals.
metadata.analysis: A week removed from leading the Rams in receiving yards, Smith fell back to Earth in a big way against Arizona, reverting back to his typical output throughout the 2025 campaign. Smith was fourth on the Rams in receiving yardage with 303 yards on 24 catches and no touchdowns. Smith's role grew as the season progressed, settling in as one of the primary backups behind starters Puka Nacua and Davante Adams (hamstring). Smith will be an exclusive-rights free agent after the postseason and will be a candidate for a one-year deal to return to the Rams as a return specialist and role player at wide receiver once again. Smith's next opportunity to produce comes in a road matchup against Carolina in the wild-card round on Saturday.

metadata.title: Xavier Smith - Full Thursday
metadata.description: Smith (chest) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
metadata.analysis: Smith led the Rams with 67 receiving yards on four catches in Monday night's loss to the Falcons. With Davante Adams (hamstring) expected to miss Week 18 against Arizona, Smith should again operate as the Rams' third receiver.

metadata.title: Xavier Smith - Limited walkthrough
metadata.description: Smith (chest) was limited at Wednesday's walkthrough, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
metadata.analysis: In Monday's 27-24 loss in Atlanta, Smith ranked third among Rams wide receivers in snap share with 51 percent behind Puka Nacua (74 percent) and Konata Mumpfield (66 percent). However, Smith paced the team with 67 receiving yards on his four catches. Assuming he's able to play through his chest injury Sunday against the Cardinals, he should continue to earn consistent looks from QB Matthew Stafford because No. 2 WR Davante Adams is expected to miss a third game in a row, as coach Sean McVay told Grosbard on Wednesday.
